label: Forêt fermée sans couvert arboré
notes: Clearcut or disturbance inside closed forest. Burnable is a judgement call: fresh logging slash is among the most flammable states a stand ever reaches, while a scraped or replanted cut carries almost nothing. The database does not say which, and gives no date. Flagged TRUE because slash is the more dangerous error.

label: Forêt fermée de feuillus purs en îlots
notes: Broadleaf islets. The dominant species is not stated, so evergreen sclerophyll stands (holm oak, cork oak) cannot be separated from deciduous ones -- a distinction that matters for flammability. Defaults to the deciduous reading, which is the more common case nationally.

label: Forêt fermée de chênes décidus purs
notes: Deciduous oak. Burnable, but leaf-off for part of the year and with a moister litter regime than the evergreen oaks -- do not treat it as equivalent to FF1G06-06.

label: Forêt fermée de chênes sempervirents purs
notes: Holm and cork oak. Given its own fuel type rather than folded into broadleaf: evergreen sclerophyllous foliage, year-round crown fuel, and typically a dense shrub understorey. This is the single most important Mediterranean fuel type the BD Forêt can resolve and CORINE cannot -- CLC 311 lumps it with beech.

label: Forêt fermée de hêtre pur
notes: Beech. Burnable but at the low end: dense shade, sparse understorey, moist litter. Kept TRUE because a burnable mask is not a flammability ranking; use fev_fuel_availability() to weight it down.

label: Forêt fermée de châtaignier pur
notes: Chestnut, usually coppiced. Coppice means a dense low stratum, so the understorey assumption embedded in 'broadleaf_closed' understates it.

label: Forêt fermée de robinier pur
notes: Black locust, usually coppiced, frequently on disturbed ground with a grassy or brambly understorey.

label: Forêt fermée d'un autre feuillu pur
notes: Catch-all for pure broadleaf stands of any other species. The species is unknown by construction, so the fuel type is a default, not a determination. Override this row if your study area has a known dominant.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange de feuillus
notes: Mixed broadleaf.

label: Forêt fermée de conifères purs en îlots
notes: Conifer islets, generally plantation.

label: Forêt fermée de pin maritime pur
notes: Maritime pine. Landes plantations: high crown fuel, and a heath or gorse understorey the database does not record.

label: Forêt fermée de pin sylvestre pur
notes: Scots pine.

label: Forêt fermée de pin laricio ou pin noir pur
notes: Laricio and black pine, largely planted, often even-aged and dense.

label: Forêt fermée de pin d'Alep pur
notes: Aleppo pine. The emblematic Mediterranean fire fuel: resinous, low crown base, serotinous regeneration, and near-systematically over a maquis or garrigue understorey that the BD Forêt cannot see.

label: Forêt fermée de pin à crochets ou pin cembro pur
notes: Mountain and Swiss stone pine, subalpine. Burnable, but in a fire regime with little in common with the lowland Mediterranean one.

label: Forêt fermée d'un autre pin pur
notes: Generic pure pine.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange de pins purs
notes: Pine mixture.

label: Forêt fermée de sapin ou épicéa
notes: Fir and spruce, mostly montane.

label: Forêt fermée de mélèze pur
notes: Larch: a deciduous conifer, so leaf-off in winter and with a grassy understorey. Treated as conifer_closed for structure, which overstates its crown fuel outside the growing season.

label: Forêt fermée de douglas pur
notes: Douglas fir plantation.

label: Forêt fermée d'un autre conifère pur autre que pin
notes: Generic pure conifer other than pine.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange d'autres conifères
notes: Mixture of conifers other than pine.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange de conifères
notes: Conifer mixture.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange de feuillus prépondérants et conifères
notes: Broadleaf-dominant mixture. Vertical mixtures raise crown continuity, which matters for torching, and neither database records it.

label: Forêt fermée à mélange de conifères prépondérants et feuillus
notes: Conifer-dominant mixture.

label: Forêt ouverte sans couvert arboré
notes: Open forest with no tree cover left. Same reasoning as FF0.

label: Forêt ouverte de feuillus purs
notes: Tree cover 10-40%, so a continuous herb or shrub stratum under the trees. This is the closest the BD Forêt gets to describing an understorey, and it is still far short of what surface spread would need.

label: Forêt ouverte de conifères purs
notes: Open conifer. Discontinuous crowns over a continuous surface fuel bed -- often more dangerous for surface spread than the closed equivalent, not less.

label: Forêt ouverte à mélange de feuillus et conifères
notes: Open mixed forest.

label: Peupleraie
notes: Poplar plantation. Given its own type: alluvial, often damp, with a grassy managed floor and no shrub layer, so it behaves nothing like the other closed broadleaf stands.

label: Lande
notes: Heath, maquis and garrigue. Non-forest but among the most flammable fuels in the Mediterranean, which is exactly why the fuel abstraction must not be restricted to forest classes.

label: Formation herbacée
notes: Herbaceous formation. Fast-drying fine fuel, rapid spread, low intensity, strongly seasonal.
